subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should maintainers require the linked SSRF socket-error PR to preserve all pinned-dispatcher security behavior and provide live IPv6-unreachable proof before accepting it, or sponsor a separate fix?
rationale: The remaining issue is real enough to keep open, but the active fix path changes the SSRF security boundary and has not yet shown safe live behavior.

options.title: Require linked PR repair and proof
options.body: Keep this issue open while the linked PR preserves DNS pinning across dispatcher modes and adds live or log proof that the IPv6-only failure rejects without gateway exit.

options.title: Sponsor a separate maintainer fix
options.body: Close or supersede the linked PR only after a maintainer-owned patch lands with the same security-boundary guarantees and proof.

options.title: Pause until live repro is available
options.body: Leave both items open but do not accept a code change until an IPv6-unreachable Docker/Linux repro is captured.

recommendation.title: Require linked PR repair and proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while the linked PR preserves DNS pinning across dispatcher modes and adds live or log proof that the IPv6-only failure rejects without gateway exit.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history signal is prior explicit-proxy SSRF pinning and adjacent network hardening work in this boundary.
